title: Saffron - Runway & Ops Prioritization Sync
summary: Quarterly health and runway check focused on usage patterns, cost drivers, latency regressions, and prioritization of runway mitigations. Agreed next steps: send model-level cost breakdown, security artifact pack, and schedule a short benchmarking session for private deployment latency tests.
next_steps: Redwood to share past 90-day per-model cost sheet and suggested quantization profiles
SE to run a 1-hour latency benchmark on Saffron's pilot VPC (tentative week of Oct 11)
CSM to coordinate executive QBR slide update for Oct 14
Customer to confirm compliance checklist items and provide expected timeline for SOC2 audit
action_items: Arjun (Redwood SE): run 1-hour latency benchmark on customer's VPC pilot - due 2027-10-14
Maya (AE): send updated pricing scenarios including reserved capacity and burst options - due 2027-10-04
Lena (CSM): update QBR deck with usage anomalies and proposed mitigations - due 2027-10-07

transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-09-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Arjun Patel (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Raj Mehta (Saffron Head of ML); Olivia Park (Infra); Dmitri Kozlov (Security); Hannah Lee (Product)

Auto-Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Usage up 2.7x during the August promo, cost spike mainly on longer ctx lengths and model variant A3-high.
- Latency regressions aligned with cache misses and batch misconfiguration.
- Customer leaning toward Dedicated for peak predictability but needs clearer TCO against Hosted + Reserved.

Topics: runway, cost, latency, dedicated vs private, security docs, benchmarks

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm gonna kick us off. quick check — is this still a good time for the 54 minute sync?
[00:07] Raj Mehta: yeah this works, we got the product folks reserved for the first half, thanks Maya.
[00:11] Lena Ortiz: great, i'll take notes for the QBR deck, tiny request, if we can get last 90 days of per model token counts that'd be super helpful.
[00:20] Arjun Patel: sure, we can pull that; quick remind-er: did you run the internal sampling filter for the promo event docs?
[00:27] Olivia Park: we did, but some of the sampling ended up hitting longer sequence lengths — so the KV cash, uh KV cache warmed up poorly, and that amplified latency.
[00:36] Dmitri Kozlov: apology — "KV cash" is my favorite mis-phrase now. But on security, we did get a couple of questions about KMS integration for Dedicated and how audit logs look when we federate with our SIEM.
[00:47] Maya Chen: great callout, we have a dedicated security pack — we'll share the SOC2 attestation plus the KMS integration guide. Arjun, any notes on the cache story?
[00:55] Arjun Patel: yeah the short version: our runtime does prefix/KV caching and it helps a lot for repeated prompts, but in your promo the prefix changed a lot so hits were low and we saw more full attention passes. also we saw batching thresholds drop because many requests were single-shot.
[01:15] Raj Mehta: that matches our telemetry.  during the promo mean sequence length jumped from 420 to about 1,200 tokens on average, which we didn't anticipate. our current cost model didn't account for that.
[01:25] Hannah Lee: question for Redwood — if we move to Dedicated pools, can we get burst capacity during promos without paying full reserved for the rest of the month?
[01:33] Maya Chen: yes, we offer burst capacity as an add-on — it's effectively a short-term quota you can spin up, priced at a higher unit rate but avoids long term commit. we can show scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[01:45] Olivia Park: any constraints on spinning bursts in our VPC pilot? like networking changes, firewall rules?
[01:52] Arjun Patel: network-wise it's just egress and port rules to the private control plane — most customers add a couple routes and we're good. for on-prem air-gap there's a different package.
[02:05] Raj Mehta: ok good. on latency, our SLAs are 95th p95 target of 120 ms for the customer-facing endpoints; we've been seeing p95 at 350 during spikes.
[02:15] Arjun Patel: noted. a couple levers: model size/quantization profile, batching window, and autoscale sensitivity. we measured that switching A3-high to A3-q4_0 trimmed about 20–30% cost and reduced latency variance. but there's a small quality delta on edge cases.
[02:40] Raj Mehta: that sounds promising but we can't tolerate hallucination increases. what does Redwood's Optimize recommend for e-com dialog workloads?
[02:48] Maya Chen: our Optimize toolkit recommends dynamic quantization profiles per route: high-quality for checkout flows, aggressive quant for browse/discovery. we can auto-route based on route tags.
[02:58] Hannah Lee: can that routing be done at the console level or is it infra only?
[03:02] Arjun Patel: yes console + SDK: you configure per-route policies, canary rollouts, and fallback to a cheaper variant if latency/CU thresholds spike.
[03:12] Dmitri Kozlov: on the compliance side, when you say "KMS integration" what exact key lifecycle do we get? rotate every n days, exportability?
[03:20] Maya Chen: we integrate with customer-managed KMS and support automatic key rotation; keys never leave the HSM, and we provide audit logs for every decryption call. we'll attach the KMS guide.
[03:30] Raj Mehta: perfect. next, the cost breakout — can you share per-model token cost and call counts? we want to attribute the August spike to specific models.
[03:38] Lena Ortiz: we already requested last 90 days — thanks — we'll add that to the QBR slides.
[03:42] Arjun Patel: quick note: the spike map points to A3-high variant and a custom rerank flow. we think a small model distillation for rerank would drop the long tail.
[03:53] Hannah Lee: distillation time? our timelines are tight.
[03:57] Arjun Patel: prototyping a distilled reranker could be 3–4 weeks with a focused POC, and then 2–3 weeks for safety/regression evals.
[04:07] Raj Mehta: hmm 6–7 weeks is ok; but we need a stopgap. any quick wins?
[04:12] Maya Chen: short wins: 1) route tagging to avoid expensive model on lower-priority routes; 2) per-route caching TTL adjustments; 3) burst pool for promos. we'll include quick implementation steps.
[04:24] Olivia Park: on route tagging — is it easy to change in prod? "live" config change?
[04:29] Arjun Patel: yes it's a config push via our console API; no full deploy required. We also support feature flags to flip routing.
[04:36] Unknown - internal PM: i had a quick question about the analytics granularity — can we get token-level costs by customer segment?
[04:42] Lena Ortiz: we can provide token-level by API key or route, should be doable. i'll put that in the items.
[04:48] Maya Chen: switching gears — security checklist: are you expecting us to ship SOC2 plus penetration test results?
[04:54] Dmitri Kozlov: yes, SOC2 is mandatory; pen test would be ideal but we can accept third-party attestations for now. also we need RBAC enforcement across teams.
[05:03] Arjun Patel: RBAC is supported at the account and team level; Console roles can be scoped to models, routes, or billing.
[05:12] Raj Mehta: excellent. to test latency for private deployment, would you prefer we give you access to the VPC pilot or do a repo-run here?
[05:20] Arjun Patel: it's faster if you provision the pilot and we run the benchmark inside your network — avoids perf fuzz from internet egress.
[05:27] Maya Chen: let's plan that — Arjun can take an action item.
[05:31] Raj Mehta: ok, timeline wise we want the results before mid-October QBR with execs.
[05:36] Maya Chen: under- stood.
[05:40] Hannah Lee: FYI finance wants to compare Dedicated reserved monthly vs hosted variable costs — do you have a TCO model?
[05:48] Maya Chen: yes, we'll send scenarios in a spreadsheet — 3, 6, 12 month comparisons with burst usage modeled.
[05:54] Olivia Park: any limitations on model version pinning in Dedicated? we have to keep a stable hash for regulatory audit.
[06:01] Arjun Patel: you can pin to a specific model version and rollback; Dedicated supports immutable model artifacts and we log every rollout with metadata for audits.
[06:12] Raj Mehta: perfect. also a tiny nit — our engineering team saw occasional request ID duplication in logs which caused a small billing mismatch.
[06:21] Arjun Patel: that sounds like a client-side retry behavior combined with idempotency token not set. we can review your client SDK usage and suggest idempotency token patterns.
[06:33] Unknown - internal PM: are there any hidden fees with burst? like data egress or extra storage fees?
[06:39] Maya Chen: standard egress applies; burst is priced per-GPU-hour and per-token usage at a higher marginal rate. we'll include it in the pricing scenarios.
[06:48] Raj Mehta: any downsides to moving some burst-only workloads to edge caching rather than dedicated GPUs?
[06:55] Arjun Patel: edge caches help for static content but less for dynamic LLM inference; the primary gains are from prefix caching and batching at the serving layer.
[07:05] Hannah Lee: can Redwood's console export the per-route tracing to our tracing system? we're on Splunk.
[07:11] Arjun Patel: yes we have tracing hooks and can ship trace spans to Splunk or other collectors; we'll share the integration guide.
[07:18] Lena Ortiz: quick housekeeping: i'll compile slides for the execs, would prefer numbers by Friday.
[07:23] Maya Chen: we'll aim to get the cost sheet and security pack by Tuesday.
[07:28] Raj Mehta: awesome. now open mic — anything else?
[07:31] Dmitri Kozlov: small ask — can you confirm data retention defaults and ability to set per-model retention to zero for regulated flows?
[07:38] Arjun Patel: yes, per-route retention controls are possible: set to zero or x days. for private deployments it's fully customer-controlled.
[07:48] Hannah Lee: timeline recap?
[07:50] Maya Chen: okay recap: Arjun does VPC benchmark week of Oct 11, Maya sends pricing by Oct 4, Lena updates QBR slide by Oct 7, Raj provides regulated model list by Oct 8. Any objections?
[08:03] Raj Mehta: no objections, sounds good.
[08:06] Maya Chen: great thanks everyone. we'll cut the recording here.

[08:10] -- End of meeting --

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribution and imperfect nouns (e.g., "KV cash" vs "KV cache"), timestamps are approximate and denote conversation time offsets.
